parts.text:
A real number is stored as the following 12-bit binary pattern:
0 1 1 0 1 0 0 0 0 0 1 1
Calculate the denary value of this number. Show your working.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Give the normalised binary pattern for +3.5. Show your working.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Give the normalised binary pattern for –3.5. Show your working.

The number of bits available to represent a real number is increased to 16.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
If the system were to use the extra 4 bits for the mantissa, state what the effect would be
on the numbers that can be represented.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
If the system were to use the extra 4 bits for the exponent instead, state what the effect
would be on the numbers that can be represented.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
A student enters the following expression into an interpreter:
OUTPUT (0.1 + 0.2)
The student is surprised to see the following output:
0.3000000000000001
Explain why this output has occurred.

optimisation. One reason is to produce code that minimises the amount of memory used.

conferencing is one of these.
